messages:
deploy-bot: :rocket: Started rollout of release v2.4.1 to canary pool (10% of traffic)
Maya R.: seeing a spike in 5xx rate on the canary group, jumping from ~0.2% -> 2.8% in the last minute
samir.k: tagged, paging on-call // incident-bot: Paging samir.k (on-call) :rotating_light:
samir.k: on it — grabbing logs now, can you paste the alert graph?
Maya R.: tried to open canary-health dashboard but it's 404? I only see generic latency charts, not success-rate by canary. dashboard/canary-health -> 404
Priya: I can try to access—also getting noisy alerts for tail-latency which look like duplicates from two different alert rules :confused:
ops-bot: alert: canary_5xx_rate > 1% (triggered)
ops-bot: alert: overall_ingress_errors > baseline_threshold (triggered)
Grace: are the canary labels propagating? might be a tagging issue that makes alerts aggregate wrong
Luis: logs show a surge of backend 502 from inference-gateway-3: `ERROR upstream read timeout` — correlates with the canary hosts that have CUDA 2.1 drivers
samir.k: pulling kube events and deployment rollout status...
Maya R.: SLO dashboard shows a ~0.7% burn on the 99.9 latency SLO for the service, but data is noisy — some datapoints missing around 12:03
Priya: hmm missing datapoints suggests we don't have the canary-specific metric exporter wired into this deploy. I think the new sidecar didn't mount metrics volume. that's why health dashboard missing
Priya: recommend kill switch and rollback if error rate persists > 1% for next 2 mins
Maya R.: confirming, 5xx rate is at 3.1% on the canary hosts now
samir.k: executing temp mitigations — flipping feature flag `v2_4_1_canary` -> off
Samir command: ```bash
# disable canary traffic
curl -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $CTRL_TOKEN" \
  https://ops-api.internal/feature_flags/v2_4_1_canary -d '{"enabled":false}'
```
ops-bot: Feature flag v2_4_1_canary set to OFF by samir.k
Maya R.: traffic back to main pool, error rate dropping to 0.4% — nice, keep observed for a bit
Priya: initiating rollback of the canary deployment to previous image (v2.4.0) to be safe
Priya command: ```bash
# rollback canary replicas to stable image
kubectl -n inference set image deploy/inference-canary inference=registry.redwood/v2.4.0 --record
```
Grace: adding note: we were alerted by canary_5xx_rate but our routing + label mismatch caused duplicate alerts (canary vs global) which drowned out the signal and slowed response. we need dedupe and a dedicated canary dashboard
Luis: also: the canary sidecar metrics mount is gated behind a new helm value `metrics.mountSidecar` — helm chart didn't include it in this release due to an old values.yaml. so metric exports were missing entirely for canary pods
Priya: actions so far: feature flag kill -> off, rollback started, paging to on-call done, no wider customer-facing incidents reported yet (observability indicates errors limited to 10% traffic in canary window)
Maya R.: customer-impact check — no support tickets yet, but a single enterprise customer reported a request timeout at 12:05 (likely routed to canary). flagged to CSMs
samir.k: monitoring SLO burn after rollback: 99.9 latency burn reduced from 0.7% -> 0.1% in last 5m. we'll keep watch for 30m
ops-bot: incident created: INC-2025-0443 (severity: high for deploy risk) — assigned to eng-release and infra teams
Grace: quick postmortem notes to capture in the ticket: missing canary dashboard, missing metrics due to helm values, duplicate/overlapping alerts, lack of a strict runbook for feature-flag kill vs immediate rollback
Luis: volunteer to drive a follow-up PR to default `metrics.mountSidecar=true` in chart and add a preflight helm check that fails deploy if canary labels not present
Priya: on-call handoff: samir.k -> Priya at 12:20 (keeping incident lead until postmortem). Priya will coordinate comms with CSMs
Maya R.: one more: add dedup rule in alerting to prevent dual firing when canary label present (`alert for service where label != canary` vs `alert for canary only`).
Priya: noted. i'll file the postmortem and assign owners: alerting dedupe (Grace), helm preflight (Luis), dashboard creation (Maya), runbook update (Priya). target: remediation PRs within 5 business days
Maya R.: thanks everyone — good catch and fast kill-switch response :thumbsup:
samir.k: leaving follow-up logs in INC ticket. will attach tracing timeline + correlation ids
ops-bot: Closing note: rollout halted for v2.4.1 until postmortem complete — schedule hold in deployment calendar
